items.q: SRNS is proteinuria despite full-dose steroid for 4 weeks; the next step, called the 1st indication in a child, is:
items.exp: Proteinuria despite full dose of steroid for 4 wk → biopsy (1st indication in child). (Book p760)

items.q: The genetic form of FSGS uncovered on biopsy carries a mutation in:
items.exp: Genetic form of FSGS (podocin mutation) → Rx: renal transplantation. (Book p760)

items.q: When biopsy shows minimal change disease in SRNS, the DOC are calcineurin inhibitors given for 6 months with a maximum duration of:
items.exp: Calcineurin inhibitors (DOC): duration 6 months; max 2 yrs. (Book p760)

items.q: Match each calcineurin-inhibitor fact with its label — 1) Tacrolimus dose 2) Tacrolimus side effects 3) Cyclosporine side effects … A) Hirsutism, gingival hyperplasia B) Neuropathy, DM, alopecia C) 0.1 mg/kg/day
items.exp: Tacrolimus 0.1 mg/kg/day with neuropathy, DM, alopecia; cyclosporine with hirsutism, gingival hyperplasia. (Book p760)

items.q: The first relapse definition in the flowchart is proteinuria appearing after:
items.exp: Relapse: proteinuria after 1 month of steroid. (Book p760)
